sample.prompt:
Define the following geoscience term:
Amorphous mineral
answer:
sample.completion: Minerals with irregular arrangement of internal particles (atoms, ions or molecules) are called crystal minerals.

question_plan.objective: Determine a worker’s posterior probability of a specified respiratory disease by integrating mineral structure, exposure-specific clinical evidence, and a positive screening result.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve interpretable diffraction findings, exposure-matched disease prevalence, and screening sensitivity and specificity, explicitly distinguishing amorphous material from crystalline material.

domain_roles.role: Identify the relevant mineral-structure category.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Amorphous mineral material has irregular internal particle arrangement rather than long-range crystalline order, correcting the sample’s erroneous crystalline label.

domain_roles.role: Translate analytical evidence into the structural classification of the inhaled material.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved diffraction criteria distinguishing amorphous and crystalline material, including limitations in detecting mixtures.

domain_roles.role: Select clinical evidence applicable to the identified exposure and screening test.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved exposure-specific disease prevalence and validated test sensitivity and specificity for a comparable worker population.

domain_roles.role: Calculate disease probability after the positive screening result.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Bayes’ theorem combining prior prevalence, sensitivity, and the false-positive rate.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Diffraction establishes the mineral structure, that classification selects the applicable clinical prior, and Bayesian updating combines that prior with screening performance.

answer_plans.plan: Interpret the diffraction evidence correctly, classify irregular internal arrangement as amorphous, select the corresponding clinical prior, and calculate the posterior using sensitivity and specificity.

Interpret the analytical evidence as showing irregular internal arrangement but omit the fact that this defines amorphous material, assigning the crystalline category instead. Apply the retrieved clinical evidence and Bayesian calculation correctly for that mistaken category.
Correctly describe the diffraction findings and amorphous structure, then independently calculate a posterior using a supplied pooled-population prior rather than the exposure-matched prior.

Correctly classify the material and select its exposure-specific prior, but treat screening sensitivity as the probability of disease given a positive result, reversing the clinical conditional probability instead of performing Bayesian updating.

chemistry.key_fact: Diffuse diffraction scattering from absent long-range atomic order
chemistry.necessity: This establishes the analytical evidence for irregular internal arrangement before the mineral-structure category is assigned.

chemistry.key_fact: Sharp Bragg diffraction peaks from periodic crystalline structure
chemistry.necessity: This supplies the contrasting diffraction criterion needed to distinguish crystalline material from disordered material.

chemistry.key_fact: Detection limits for crystalline fractions in amorphous–crystalline mixtures
chemistry.necessity: This prevents absent detectable crystalline peaks from being treated as proof that the inhaled material contains no crystalline component.

medical.key_fact: Respiratory disease prevalence stratified by amorphous versus crystalline exposure
medical.necessity: Exposure-stratified prevalence provides both the appropriate clinical prior and the alternative prior selected after mistaken structural classification.

medical.key_fact: Pooled worker-population respiratory disease prevalence across exposure categories
medical.necessity: The parallel-knowledge answer needs a supplied pooled prior that bypasses the exposure-specific clinical link.

medical.key_fact: Screening sensitivity and specificity validated in comparable exposed workers
medical.necessity: Applicable screening-performance estimates support valid updating and supply the sensitivity misinterpreted in the conditional-reversal answer.

mathematics.key_fact: Bayesian positive predictive value from prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity
mathematics.necessity: Bayes’ theorem calculates the posterior using either the appropriate prior or the deliberately substituted prior.

mathematics.key_fact: Total positive probability as sensitivity-weighted prevalence plus false-positive-weighted nonprevalence
mathematics.necessity: This constructs the Bayesian denominator using one minus specificity as the false-positive rate and one minus prevalence as the nondisease probability.

mathematics.key_fact: Conditional-probability reversal between positive given disease and disease given positive
mathematics.necessity: This distinguishes sensitivity from the requested posterior and identifies why substituting sensitivity for that posterior is invalid.

sample.prompt:
Define the following geoscience term:
Alluvium
answer:
sample.completion: Sediments formed by mechanical sedimentation of rivers.

question_plan.objective: Identify the alluvial drinking-water well with the greatest probability of exceeding a chronic inorganic-arsenic exposure benchmark.
question_plan.conditions: Later samples must provide contrasting sediment origins, well-specific arsenic species fractions and lognormal total-concentration parameters, daily water intake, body mass, an applicable chronic oral benchmark, and normal-CDF values.

domain_roles.role: Determine which wells satisfy the alluvial-aquifer requirement.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Alluvium consists of sediments mechanically deposited by rivers, unlike deposits formed by other processes.

domain_roles.role: Convert total arsenic concentrations into concentrations of the benchmark-relevant chemical species.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved arsenic-speciation evidence must establish the inorganic fraction for each well and its applicability to the concentration measurements.

domain_roles.role: Translate the chronic oral exposure benchmark into a person-specific drinking-water concentration threshold.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved toxicological guidance must establish the applicable inorganic-arsenic benchmark, exposure assumptions, and body-mass-normalized dose relationship.

domain_roles.role: Calculate and compare benchmark-exceedance probabilities.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Scaling a lognormal concentration distribution and evaluating its upper-tail probability at a specified threshold.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Filter wells by mechanical river deposition, combine arsenic speciation with intake and body mass to derive dose distributions, and rank their benchmark-exceedance probabilities.

answer_plans.plan: Restrict consideration to alluvial wells, scale each total-concentration distribution by its inorganic fraction and intake-to-body-mass ratio, and select the greatest probability of exceeding the retrieved chronic benchmark.
Correctly identify alluvial wells and apply the medical dose relationship and lognormal calculation, but omit arsenic speciation by treating all measured arsenic as inorganic.

Correctly identify alluvium, describe inorganic arsenic toxicity, report species fractions, and calculate mean total concentrations separately, but prioritize the highest mean without integrating these facts into exposure-exceedance probabilities.

Use the correct alluvial classification, species fractions, medical benchmark, and probability method, but multiply rather than divide the allowable total-concentration threshold by the inorganic fraction, reversing how speciation affects risk.

chemistry.key_fact: Inorganic arsenic comprises arsenite As(III) and arsenate As(V)
chemistry.necessity: Identifies which measured arsenic species count toward the inorganic-arsenic benchmark.

chemistry.key_fact: Well-specific inorganic fraction equals inorganic arsenic divided by total arsenic on an elemental-As mass basis
chemistry.necessity: Provides comparable species fractions for converting each well's total arsenic measurements into benchmark-relevant concentrations.

chemistry.key_fact: Constant representative inorganic fraction gives C_inorganic = f_inorganic × C_total
chemistry.necessity: Establishes when a fixed fraction applies across a well's concentration distribution and why the allowable total concentration must be divided, not multiplied, by that fraction.

medical.key_fact: Chronic oral inorganic-arsenic reference dose and its noncancer toxicity basis
medical.necessity: Supplies an applicable numerical exposure benchmark and toxicity context without equating benchmark exceedance with disease probability.

medical.key_fact: Person-specific daily drinking-water intake, body mass, and chronic exposure assumptions
medical.necessity: Provides the exposure inputs and duration assumptions needed to apply a chronic body-mass-normalized benchmark to the modeled water concentrations.

medical.key_fact: Waterborne oral dose D = C_inorganic × intake / body mass
medical.necessity: With consistent units and a stated treatment of other exposure sources, converts the dose benchmark into a person-specific inorganic-arsenic concentration threshold.

mathematics.key_fact: Lognormal parameters ln C ~ N(μ, σ²) and positive scaling μ_scaled = μ + ln k
mathematics.necessity: Defines each well's concentration distribution and permits fixed speciation and intake-to-body-mass factors to transform it into a dose distribution.

mathematics.key_fact: Lognormal upper tail P(C > T) = 1 − Φ((ln T − μ)/σ)
mathematics.necessity: Uses normal-CDF values to calculate and rank benchmark-exceedance probabilities for eligible wells.

mathematics.key_fact: Lognormal mean E[C] = exp(μ + σ²/2) does not determine upper-tail ranking
mathematics.necessity: Supports the separate mean-total-concentration calculation while explaining why ranking those means cannot replace exposure-exceedance comparisons.

sample.prompt:
question:
Gause's principle explains that
options:
A.populations are independent of resource consumption
B.no two species can fill the same niche at the same time
C.organisms adapt and reproduce in a changing environment
D.genetic changes are never random
E.all living things are grouped into species or separate types
answer:
sample.completion: B.no two species can fill the same niche at the same time

question_plan.objective: Select a medically eligible chelator–probiotic candidate predicted to exclude a pathogen through resource competition in a gut-mimicking chemostat.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve evidence of shared limiting-resource dependence, nutrient-binding equilibria and complex bioavailability, growth and dilution parameters, and patient-specific safety restrictions.

domain_roles.role: Explain pathogen exclusion through competition for the same niche.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Gause's principle excludes stable coexistence of complete competitors under constant conditions without niche differentiation.

domain_roles.role: Determine the nutrient pool accessible to each competitor after chelation.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Binding equilibria, chemical mass balances, and evidence establishing whether either organism can use the nutrient–chelator complex.

domain_roles.role: Determine which organism persists under the supplied chemostat model.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Break-even resource concentrations and invasion or washout conditions derived from the supplied growth equations.

domain_roles.role: Restrict selection to candidates medically eligible for the specified patient.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved contraindications and safety restrictions for the proposed probiotic and chelator.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Chemical bioavailability feeds the competition model, Gause's principle interprets exclusion, and medical restrictions determine whether the predicted winner supports an eligible candidate.

answer_plans.plan: Use nutrient speciation and accessibility to calculate persistence and invasion outcomes, selecting a medically eligible candidate in which the probiotic persists and the pathogen cannot invade. Interpret this as model-based competitive exclusion, not established clinical efficacy.

Omit the retrieved fact that the nutrient–chelator complex is inaccessible to both organisms and instead count total nutrient as usable, while correctly applying the competition equations, exclusion principle, and medical restrictions.

State speciation, unchelated competition outcomes, Gause's principle, and medical eligibility correctly in isolation, but select a candidate without recalculating competition using chelation-altered nutrient availability.

Calculate accessible nutrient and break-even concentrations correctly and respect medical restrictions, but reverse the competitive relationship by treating the organism requiring more limiting nutrient as the resource-competition winner.

chemistry.key_fact: Nutrient–chelator formation constants and equilibrium speciation
chemistry.necessity: Binding equilibria determine how chelation partitions the limiting nutrient between free and complexed forms.

chemistry.key_fact: Nutrient and chelator mass balances across free and complexed forms
chemistry.necessity: Mass balances connect supplied total concentrations to the equilibrium concentrations needed to calculate accessible nutrient.

chemistry.key_fact: Nutrient–chelator complex inaccessible to both competing organisms
chemistry.necessity: This accessibility condition excludes complexed nutrient from the usable pool and identifies the fact omitted when total nutrient is incorrectly counted as available.

mathematics.key_fact: Break-even resource concentration defined by growth rate equaling dilution rate
mathematics.necessity: Solving μ_i(R_i*) = D gives each organism's resource requirement under the supplied chemostat growth equations.

mathematics.key_fact: Washout when growth at the accessible resource supply cannot exceed dilution
mathematics.necessity: This condition tests whether the probiotic can persist after chelation rather than assuming that suppressing the pathogen guarantees probiotic survival.

mathematics.key_fact: Lower break-even resource wins feasible single-resource competition; invasion requires positive net growth
mathematics.necessity: Evaluating pathogen growth at the probiotic's equilibrium resource concentration establishes exclusion and exposes the reversed winner relationship in the incorrect answer.

medical.key_fact: Probiotic-associated bloodstream infection risk in severely immunocompromised patients
medical.necessity: Patient susceptibility and candidate-specific safety evidence are needed to determine whether a proposed live probiotic is medically eligible.

medical.key_fact: Agent-specific chelator contraindications and restrictions in renal or hepatic impairment
medical.necessity: The proposed chelator's documented restrictions must be checked against patient organ function before selecting an otherwise successful candidate.

medical.key_fact: In vitro pathogen exclusion does not establish clinical efficacy
medical.necessity: This evidence boundary prevents a chemostat prediction from being presented as demonstrated therapeutic benefit.

question_plan.conditions: Later retrieval must supply applicable refugee and program eligibility rules, hypothetical individual persecution and flight histories, clinically supported treatment benefits, referral costs, and a budget yielding a unique optimum.

domain_roles.role: Interpret the displacement context and the identity basis of reported targeting.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retain the sample’s classification as an ethnic conflict and obtain the geographic information needed to distinguish internal displacement from cross-border flight.

domain_roles.role: Determine which individuals qualify for the specified referral program.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve applicable refugee criteria, the treatment of ethnicity under protected persecution grounds, and program rules without assuming conflict exposure alone establishes eligibility.

domain_roles.role: Determine the expected health benefit of referring each eligible individual.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve condition-specific evidence about treatment effectiveness, urgency, and the consequences of delayed care.

domain_roles.role: Select the eligible cohort with the greatest total expected health benefit within the budget.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Use binary constrained optimization with individual referral costs and medically derived benefit values.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Use ethnic targeting and flight geography to apply legal eligibility criteria, then optimize medically supported benefits only across eligible referrals.

answer_plans.plan: Retain the ethnic-conflict classification, assess each person’s flight and persecution evidence under the supplied legal rules, and calculate medically supported benefits. Select the eligible combination maximizing total benefit within the referral budget.

Correctly interpret ethnic targeting and cross-border movement, calculate medical benefits, and optimize the budget, but omit the required individual persecution criterion and treat every cross-border conflict survivor as eligible.

Correctly report the ethnic-conflict context, legal eligibility findings, medical benefits, and an unrestricted budget optimum separately. Recommend that unrestricted optimum without incorporating the legal eligibility findings into the optimization.

Use the relevant geographic, legal, clinical, and optimization facts, but treat high medical benefit as establishing the protected-ground persecution nexus. Optimize referrals after this mistaken substitution expands the eligible pool.

legal.key_fact: Refugee criteria requiring presence outside the country of nationality and a well-founded fear of persecution
legal.necessity: These criteria connect flight histories to individual eligibility and expose why cross-border conflict exposure alone is insufficient.

legal.key_fact: Ethnic targeting as persecution on race or nationality grounds, requiring an evidenced nexus

legal.key_fact: Program-specific referral eligibility requirements and exclusions
legal.necessity: The supplied program rules determine which legally assessed individuals may enter the referral selection pool.

medical.key_fact: Condition-specific treatment effectiveness and patient-specific contraindications
medical.necessity: Clinical evidence establishes whether each proposed referral can deliver the anticipated treatment benefit.

medical.key_fact: Risk of death or irreversible morbidity from delaying condition-specific care
medical.necessity: Delay-related prognosis supplies the clinical consequences of not referring an individual within the program's treatment window.

medical.key_fact: Patient-specific expected health gains from referral versus non-referral on a common clinical outcome scale
medical.necessity: Comparable incremental benefits provide the optimization values without supplying evidence of legally protected persecution.

mathematics.key_fact: Binary referral selection with eligibility constraints x_i ≤ e_i
mathematics.necessity: Eligibility indicators translate legal findings into selection restrictions, distinguishing omitted gates from incorrectly assigned eligibility.

mathematics.key_fact: Referral feasibility constraints Σc_i x_i ≤ B and Σx_i ≤ K
mathematics.necessity: Individual costs, total budget, and referral capacity determine which candidate cohorts are operationally feasible.

mathematics.key_fact: Additive benefit maximization with a strict objective gap over every alternative feasible cohort
mathematics.necessity: Comparing total benefits establishes a unique optimum and permits comparison with optima produced by dropping or misassigning eligibility restrictions.

sample.prompt:
question:
A city is located on a river that is prone to flooding yet provides trade advantages that bring measurable wealth to the city. Based on this information, which of the following statements would best fit that city?
options:
A.The city has a good site yet a poor situation.
B.The city has a good situation yet a poor site.
C.The city has a good situation and a good site.
D.The city has flood disadvantages that outweigh the trade advantages.
E.The city has trade advantages that outweigh the flood disadvantages
answer:
sample.completion: B.The city has a good situation yet a poor site.

question_plan.objective: Choose the legally permissible flood-management investment with the highest expected NPV while explaining how it addresses the city's poor site without sacrificing its good situation.
question_plan.conditions: Later retrieval must supply an applicable floodway permitting rule, project-specific hydraulic effects, conditional flood probabilities, damage estimates, retained trade benefits, costs, project lives, and a discount rate.

domain_roles.role: Distinguish the local flood hazard targeted by investment from the river-trade connectivity worth preserving.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Flood exposure indicates a poor site, whereas advantageous trade connections indicate a good situation.

domain_roles.role: Determine which investments are permissible before comparing their financial value.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: A retrieved jurisdiction-specific floodway permitting rule and its application to each project's modeled hydraulic effects.

domain_roles.role: Rank permissible investments by expected incremental NPV relative to a stated baseline.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Discounting of retained trade benefits, avoided expected flood losses, operating costs, and initial investment.

domain_roles.role: Convert conditional flood-event data into annual expected losses for each investment.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: The law of total probability and probability-weighted losses across mutually exclusive event outcomes.

question_plan.reasoning_link: The site–situation distinction identifies losses and benefits, probability calculations quantify flood losses, legal rules filter projects, and discounted cash flows select the best admissible response.

answer_plans.plan: Identify a poor site and good situation, calculate expected flood losses from the event tree, exclude legally impermissible projects, and select the remaining investment with the highest incremental NPV.
Use the geographic distinction, event probabilities, and NPV calculations correctly but omit the applicable permitting restriction, selecting a higher-NPV project that fails it.

State the geographic classification, legal eligibility, expected flood losses, and discounted trade values correctly in isolation, but rank eligible projects using trade-only NPV without incorporating the calculated flood losses.
Calculate probabilities and NPV correctly and recognize the permitting restriction, but treat positive financial value from the good situation as overriding that legal restriction.

legal.key_fact: Applicable floodway encroachment limits and permitting exceptions
legal.necessity: The jurisdiction-specific rule establishes which projects are permissible and identifies the restriction omitted by the missing-knowledge answer.

legal.key_fact: Hydraulic-model evidence required to demonstrate floodway compliance
legal.necessity: The required evidence connects each project's modeled hydraulic effects to the applicable permit threshold and any exception conditions.

legal.key_fact: Mandatory permit conditions cannot be overridden by positive NPV
legal.necessity: This relationship makes legal eligibility a prerequisite to financial selection rather than a restriction that trade benefits can outweigh.

financial.key_fact: Incremental cash flows from trade benefits, avoided flood losses, and operating costs
financial.necessity: Baseline-relative cash flows integrate preserved trade with flood-risk reduction and expose the parallel answer's omission of calculated flood losses.

financial.key_fact: Expected NPV from initial investment and discounted project-life cash flows
financial.necessity: Initial costs, cash-flow timing, project lives, and the discount rate are needed to calculate comparable present values.

financial.key_fact: Highest incremental NPV selection among feasible alternatives
financial.necessity: This decision rule ranks investments after eligibility screening and distinguishes the admissible optimum from an unrestricted or trade-only ranking.

mathematics.key_fact: Event-tree path probabilities as products of conditional probabilities
mathematics.necessity: Project-specific conditional flood data must be converted into joint outcome probabilities without incorrectly assuming independence.

mathematics.key_fact: Total probability over mutually exclusive and exhaustive scenarios
mathematics.necessity: Summing the relevant event-tree paths yields unconditional annual flood probabilities without double-counting outcomes.

mathematics.key_fact: Expected annual loss as the sum of outcome probabilities times damages
mathematics.necessity: Outcome-specific damage estimates and probabilities produce baseline and project losses whose differences enter the financial comparison.

domain_roles.role: Determine which locations satisfy the gravity flow's provenance requirements.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Gravity-flow formation requires an available sediment source, assessed from supplied geomorphic evidence rather than water depth alone.

domain_roles.role: Translate sediment fingerprints into chemically valid source-mixing constraints.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Conservative tracer selection and the appropriate concentration-dependent mixing relationship.

domain_roles.role: Infer source proportions under all eligibility and chemical constraints.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Constrained linear inversion with nonnegative proportions summing to one and verification of solution uniqueness.

domain_roles.role: Determine which candidate sources can deliver sediment through the supplied network.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Directed graph reachability after removing transport-blocking edges.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Geographic source eligibility and graph reachability restrict the variables in the chemically derived mixing system before mathematical inversion.

answer_plans.plan: Exclude locations lacking available sediment or an unblocked downstream path, then solve the chemically valid constrained mixing system for the unique source proportions.
Use correct tracer chemistry, graph reachability, and constrained inversion, but admit a chemically matching location whose supplied geomorphic evidence shows no available sediment.

Report correct sediment-availability classifications, network reachability, and an unrestricted chemical mixing solution independently, without applying the geographic and network results as constraints on that solution.
Apply the correct provenance criteria and chemical inversion, but qualify sources using paths from the deposit to each source rather than sediment-delivery paths from each source to the deposit.

chemistry.key_fact: Conservative sediment tracers unaffected by reaction or fractionation
chemistry.necessity: Tracer conservation is required for deposit chemistry to retain interpretable source fingerprints.

chemistry.key_fact: Source-endmember and deposit tracer concentrations on a common mass basis
chemistry.necessity: These measurements supply chemically comparable fingerprints and the observed mixture composition.

chemistry.key_fact: Mass-weighted concentration mixing and denominator-abundance-weighted ratio mixing
chemistry.necessity: The appropriate mass-balance relationship prevents treating concentration-dependent tracer ratios as simple averages of sediment proportions.

mathematics.key_fact: Nonnegative mixture proportions summing to one
mathematics.necessity: Simplex constraints distinguish physically admissible proportions from arbitrary algebraic solutions.

mathematics.key_fact: Restricted linear inversion with excluded-source coefficients fixed to zero
mathematics.necessity: This incorporates source-eligibility decisions into the mixing equations and distinguishes integrated inversion from an unrestricted parallel solution.

mathematics.key_fact: Feasibility and singleton-solution verification for constrained linear systems
mathematics.necessity: Checking the constrained feasible set establishes whether the selected sources yield exactly one admissible mixture.

computer_science.key_fact: Directed reachability from candidate source to deposit
computer_science.necessity: Directed paths encode delivery eligibility, while reversing their endpoints creates the specified incorrect relation.
Removing unusable edges prevents nominal connections from being counted as operational transport paths.

computer_science.key_fact: Breadth-first or depth-first search for a reachability mask
computer_science.necessity: Traversal produces explicit per-source reachability results that can constrain inversion or be reported independently in the parallel answer.

question:
The United Nations developed a metric by which the health of a nation can be judged. It measures standard of living, longevity, and access to education. The name of this metric is
options:
A.the Global Peace Index
B.the Human Development Index
C.the Genuine Progress Indicator
D.the Social Progress Index
E.the Gross National Happiness Index
answer:

key_facts: standard of living, longevity, education access

question_plan.objective: Identify the UN development metric and select the health program producing its greatest improvement within a present-value funding limit.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve program-specific mortality projections, life-table methods, education and income inputs, UNDP formulas, payment schedules, and discounting assumptions that make the funding limit consequential.

domain_roles.role: Identify the Human Development Index and its relevant development dimensions.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: HDI measures longevity, education, and standard of living using UNDP-defined indicators.

domain_roles.role: Translate each program's projected mortality effects into the longevity input.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Life-table methods connect age-specific all-cause mortality to life expectancy at birth.

domain_roles.role: Determine which programs satisfy the funding constraint.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Discounted cash-flow valuation converts scheduled program payments into comparable present-value costs.

domain_roles.role: Calculate and compare projected HDI improvements.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Apply the supplied normalization rules and geometric-mean aggregation to the dimension indices.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Medical projections determine HDI longevity changes, financial valuation filters feasible programs, and mathematical aggregation ranks their overall development gains.

answer_plans.plan: Identify HDI, derive life expectancy from projected mortality, and calculate each program's HDI gain using the supplied formulas. Select the greatest gain among programs whose discounted payments satisfy the funding limit.

Omit the life-table relationship and substitute disease-specific survival improvement for the change in life expectancy at birth. Otherwise identify HDI, apply its formulas, and enforce the discounted funding limit correctly.
Correctly calculate projected HDI gains and present-value costs separately, but recommend the largest HDI gain without restricting the ranking to financially feasible programs.

Correctly derive longevity and program present values, but subtract program present-value costs directly from the supplied national income input before calculating HDI. This incorrectly treats a financing constraint as an established change in the standard-of-living indicator.

medical.key_fact: Program-specific changes in age-specific all-cause mortality
medical.necessity: These projections supply the mortality inputs needed to estimate each program's population-wide longevity effects.

medical.key_fact: Life-table life expectancy at birth from survivorship and person-years lived
medical.necessity: This relationship converts projected mortality into the required longevity input and identifies the step omitted by the missing-knowledge answer.

medical.key_fact: Disease-specific survival gains are not equivalent to population life-expectancy gains
medical.necessity: This distinction establishes why substituting a disease-specific survival improvement for a change in life expectancy is invalid.

financial.key_fact: Payment-schedule present value using time-matched discount rates
financial.necessity: Scheduled payments and consistent discounting assumptions are needed to calculate comparable program costs at a common valuation date.

financial.key_fact: Present-value budget feasibility requires discounted costs not exceeding the funding limit
financial.necessity: This rule filters eligible programs before ranking gains and exposes the parallel answer's failure to enforce the constraint.

financial.key_fact: Program financing outlays do not automatically reduce national income
financial.necessity: This accounting distinction prevents treating discounted program expenditure as an established reduction in the supplied income indicator.

mathematics.key_fact: Affine normalization of longevity and schooling inputs, with arithmetic averaging of schooling indices
mathematics.necessity: These transformations convert life expectancy and the two schooling inputs into comparable dimension indices using the supplied bounds.

mathematics.key_fact: Logarithmic income normalization between specified lower and upper bounds
mathematics.necessity: This transformation computes the income dimension and makes the consequences of incorrectly altering its input calculable.

mathematics.key_fact: Three-index geometric-mean aggregation and baseline-relative gain comparison
mathematics.necessity: The cube root of the dimension-index product gives each projected score, whose difference from baseline supplies the gain used for program ranking.

sample.prompt:
question:
The water that does not participate in crystal composition and has nothing to do with mineral crystals is:
Choose from:

A. Zeolite water
B. Combined water
C. Interlayer water
D. Adsorbed water
answer:

question_plan.objective: Identify the non-crystal water in a mineral feed and select the drying regime that removes it selectively while maximizing project net present value.
question_plan.conditions: Later samples must supply mineral-specific desorption and structural-water temperature limits, a validated first-order drying model with parameters, target moisture, operating hours, costs, revenues, project life, and discount rate.

domain_roles.role: Identify the water fraction that the drying process should remove.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Adsorbed water lies outside mineral crystal composition, unlike water incorporated into mineral structures.

domain_roles.role: Determine which drying regimes remove the target water without removing structural water.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved mineral-specific thermal selectivity limits and temperature-dependent desorption parameters.

domain_roles.role: Calculate drying time and achievable throughput for each chemically admissible regime.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Integration of the supplied first-order moisture-loss differential equation and conversion of batch duration into annual throughput.

domain_roles.role: Rank admissible regimes by their economic value over the project lifetime.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Conversion of throughput into net cash flows and discounted-cash-flow calculation of net present value.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Water classification determines chemical admissibility, drying kinetics determine throughput, and throughput-dependent discounted cash flows determine the preferred regime.

answer_plans.plan: Identify adsorbed water, exclude regimes that remove structural water, solve the supplied drying model, and choose the admissible regime with the highest throughput-adjusted net present value.
Correctly identify adsorbed water, enforce chemical selectivity, and calculate throughput, but omit discounting and rank regimes using undiscounted lifetime net cash flows.

Correctly identify the water, establish safe temperatures, solve drying times, and state the net-present-value method, but evaluate cash flows using identical assumed throughput instead of the calculated drying-dependent throughput.

Use the supplied kinetics and financial calculations consistently, but treat the onset of structural-water removal as the minimum temperature required to remove adsorbed water, thereby applying the chemical constraint in the wrong direction.

chemistry.key_fact: Mineral-specific temperature conditions for adsorbed-water desorption
chemistry.necessity: These conditions establish when the target water can be removed without assuming that structural-water removal is required.

chemistry.key_fact: Structural-water loss onset as an upper thermal selectivity boundary
chemistry.necessity: This boundary excludes structurally damaging regimes and identifies the constraint that the incorrect-relation answer reverses.

chemistry.key_fact: Validated first-order desorption kinetics with temperature-dependent rate constants
chemistry.necessity: The applicable kinetic law and mineral-specific parameters connect drying temperature to moisture-removal speed.

mathematics.key_fact: Exponential solution of the first-order moisture-loss differential equation
mathematics.necessity: Integrating the supplied equation gives moisture as a function of time for each regime.

mathematics.key_fact: Logarithmic inversion of exponential decay for finite target-reaching time
mathematics.necessity: This inversion calculates drying duration and checks whether the target lies above any asymptotic moisture limit.

mathematics.key_fact: Annual throughput as batch quantity times operating hours divided by cycle duration
mathematics.necessity: This conversion links calculated drying times to production volumes, a link deliberately left unused in the parallel-knowledge answer.

financial.key_fact: Throughput-dependent operating cash flow from sales revenue minus operating costs
financial.necessity: This relationship translates production into regime-specific cash flows and exposes the error of assuming identical throughput.

financial.key_fact: Net present value as discounted project cash flows minus initial investment
financial.necessity: The project life and discount rate are needed to value cash flows at a common date rather than merely sum them.

financial.key_fact: Maximum-NPV selection versus undiscounted lifetime cash-flow ranking
financial.necessity: This decision rule selects the best admissible regime and distinguishes the intended financial criterion from the missing-financial-knowledge substitute.

question:
The reason for the strong folding of the rock stratum is
answer:

question_plan.objective: Select the tunnel alignment with the lowest discounted excavation and drainage-treatment cost through strongly folded rock strata.
question_plan.conditions: Later samples must supply surveyed folded-bed boundaries, candidate alignments, mineral distributions, drainage-reaction assumptions, treatment requirements, costs, schedules, and a discount rate.

domain_roles.role: Interpret the folded strata and their repeated intersections along tunnel alignments.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Strong horizontal compression causes strong folding, and mapped folded beds can intersect an alignment repeatedly.

domain_roles.role: Calculate each alignment's excavation volume within reactive rock beds.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Line–boundary intersections, summed segment lengths, and tunnel cross-sectional geometry.

domain_roles.role: Convert reactive-rock exposure into drainage-treatment requirements.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved mineral-specific acid-generation reactions, neutralization stoichiometry, and assumptions linking excavated material to drainage loads.

domain_roles.role: Compare the present value of excavation and treatment expenditures.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Discounted lifecycle cost analysis for differently timed cash outflows.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Compression-produced fold geometry determines reactive-rock quantities, which determine chemical treatment loads and ultimately discounted alignment costs.

answer_plans.plan: Attribute strong folding to horizontal compression, calculate all mapped reactive-bed intersections, and derive treatment quantities using the supplied chemistry. Select the alignment with the lowest discounted total cost.
Use the compression interpretation, intersection calculations, and treatment chemistry correctly, but omit discounting and select the alignment with the lowest undiscounted expenditure.

State the folding cause, calculate intersection volumes, describe treatment chemistry, and discount costs correctly in isolation. Apply the same treatment load to every alignment instead of linking each alignment's reactive-rock volume to its chemical load.

Recognize compression-driven folding and use valid geometric, chemical, and discounting methods, but apply the acid-generation calculation to nonreactive-bed volumes rather than reactive-bed volumes. Rank alignments using the resulting misassigned treatment costs.

mathematics.key_fact: Alignment–boundary intersections ordered by distance along the tunnel
mathematics.necessity: These intersections locate every entry and exit where an alignment crosses mapped bed boundaries.

mathematics.key_fact: Summation of disjoint alignment-segment lengths within labeled regions
mathematics.necessity: Summing separately labeled intervals accounts for repeated crossings while preserving the distinction between reactive and nonreactive beds.

mathematics.key_fact: Excavation volume as cross-sectional area integrated along alignment segments
mathematics.necessity: This converts each alignment's bed-intersection lengths into the rock volumes needed for excavation costing and chemical-load calculations.

chemistry.key_fact: Mineral-specific acid-generation reactions and stoichiometric acid yields
chemistry.necessity: These reactions identify which minerals generate acidity under the supplied conditions and distinguish reactive material from material incorrectly assigned an acid load.

chemistry.key_fact: Rock-volume-to-drainage-load conversion using density, mineral abundance, reacted fraction, and release timing
chemistry.necessity: This links each alignment's reactive-rock quantity to its own time-dependent drainage load, exposing both identical-load and wrong-bed assignments.

chemistry.key_fact: Neutralizer dosage from acid equivalents, reagent capacity, and required treatment endpoint
chemistry.necessity: This converts predicted acidity into reagent requirements that satisfy the supplied drainage-treatment standard.

financial.key_fact: Scheduled cash outflows from excavation and treatment quantities multiplied by applicable unit costs
financial.necessity: This translates alignment-specific physical requirements into expenditures at the times when excavation and treatment occur.

financial.key_fact: Present value of a time-t expenditure as C_t divided by (1+r)^t
financial.necessity: Discounting makes differently timed expenditures comparable and defines the financial step omitted by the missing-domain answer.

financial.key_fact: Least-cost alignment selection by summed discounted lifecycle expenditures over a common horizon
financial.necessity: This supplies the final ranking rule and distinguishes minimum present-value cost from minimum undiscounted expenditure.
